FOOTNOTES

2/ Pursuant to A.R.S. § 26-306.02, this appropriation is exempt from the provisions of A.R.S. § 35-190, relating to lapsing of appropriations; however, any unexpended monies shall be used to reduce the assessment and appropriation in future years.

4/ In addition to any other appropriations made in fiscal year 2026-2027, the Arizona department of agriculture may spend up to \$250,000 from the commercial feed trust fund established by section 3-2607, Arizona Revised Statutes, in fiscal year 2026-2027 for expenses related to the avian influenza outbreak. (General Appropriations Act footnote)   
5/ General Appropriations Act funds are appropriated as an Operating Lump Sum with Special Line Items by Agency.

Operating Budget

The Baseline includes \$17,249,500 and 215.4 FTE Positions in FY 2027 for the operating budget. These amounts consist of:

General Fund \$15,619,200

Air Quality Fund 1,630,300

Adjustments are as follows:

Remove One-Time Appropriations

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(381,100) from the General Fund in FY 2027 for removal of one-time funding for equipment purchases associated with hiring 5 new staff.

Agriculture and Water Innovation Fund Deposit

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for an Agriculture and Water Innovation Fund deposit. Adjustments are as follows:
section_path: Agriculture and Water Innovation Fund Deposit

text:
Remove One-Time Funding

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(2,000,000) from the Long-Term Water Augmentation Fund in FY 2027 for removal of a one-time deposit to the non-appropriated Agriculture and Water Innovation Fund.

The FY 2026 Environment Budget Reconciliation Bill (BRB) established this fund for a pilot program to award grants for the installation of agriculture water efficiency technology to farming entities or irrigation districts (on behalf of its members) that meet the statutory qualifications. In addition to the deposit, the fund may also receive federal grants.

Agricultural Consulting and Training

The Baseline includes \$135,700 from the General Fund in FY 2027 for the Agricultural Consulting and Training line item. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

This line item funds on-site visits to establishments for consultation, interpreting, and applying alternative methods of complying with statutes, rules, regulations, and standards relating to compliance.

Agricultural Employment Relations Board

The Baseline includes \$23,300 from the General Fund in FY 2027 for the Agricultural Employment Relations Board line item. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026. This line item funds accounting and budgeting support for the Agricultural Employment Relations Board. The board receives and investigates complaints and conducts farm labor union elections.

Animal Damage Control

The Baseline includes \$65,000 from the General Fund in FY 2027 for the Animal Damage Control line item. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

This line item funds agreements with the U.S. Department of Agriculture to control, dispatch, or relocate predatory animals and noxious rodents, which are injurious to livestock, poultry, agriculture, other industries, or the public health.

Nuclear Emergency Management Program

The Baseline includes \$352,900 and 2.44 FTE Positions from the Nuclear Emergency Management Fund (NEMF) in FY 2027 for the Nuclear Emergency Management Program line item. Adjustments are as follows:

New NEMF Assessment

The Baseline includes an increase of \$5,800 from the NEMF in FY 2027 for a change to the assessment rate in FY 2027.

Laws 2025, Chapter 56 (as amended by Laws 2025, Chapter 238) appropriated \$347,109 and 2.44 FTE Positions from NEMF in FY 2026 and \$352,877 and 2.44 FTE Positions from NEMF in FY 2027. As a result, these monies do not appear in the General Appropriation Act. (Please see Table 1 below for more information.)

The Legislature is required to biennially assess a fee against each group of public service and municipal corporations operating the Palo Verde Nuclear Generating Station. The fee is set at a level to offset the NEMF appropriation. The Legislature enacts this revised fee level in a bill outside of the budget process.

Monies in the NEMF are used for the development and maintenance of a state plan for off-site responses to an emergency caused by an accident at a commercial nuclear generating station. NEMF monies are also used to provide for the equipment, personnel, facilities, training and testing necessary to comply with federally prescribed criteria.

Department representatives assist in the planning for offsite responses to an emergency at the Palo Verde Nuclear Generating Station and participate in the annual response exercises, mainly the Ingestion Pathway Zone exercises. The Department of Agriculture is responsible for controlling embargoes of food, water, and milk in the event that there is an emergency that would contaminate those items produced in the areas around the plant.

Red Imported Fire Ant Control

The Baseline includes \$23,200 from the General Fund in FY 2027 for the Red Imported Fire Ant Control line item. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

This line item funds ongoing pest exclusion efforts aimed at preventing the introduction of the red imported fire ant. The state has successfully suppressed isolated infestations of red imported fire ants and continues to be federally certified as free from this pest.

Information Technology Projects and Cloud Migration

The FY 2026 budget included a footnote extending the \$2,000,000 FY 2023 appropriation from the General Fund for the Department of Agriculture's Information Technology (IT) projects and cloud migration from the end of FY 2026 to the end of FY 2027. (Please see the Department of Administration - Automation Projects Fund narrative for details regarding the Department of Agriculture's IT projects.)
